key_insight: MedGemma with structured radiologist descriptors met the prespecified non-inferiority criterion versus EU-TIRADS for thyroid nodule malignancy discrimination; configurations without those descriptors performed worse.
clinical_relevance: This diagnostic AI study—not drug discovery—suggests potential to reduce false positives, but with additional missed cancers and no demonstrated advantage over EU-TIRADS ≥5.
method: Retrospective thyroid ultrasound study using two Tunisian centers and selected public-dataset images.
Fine-tuned MedGemma 1.5 4B across four input configurations, with patient-level training, validation and sealed test splits.
Compared performance against expert-rated EU-TIRADS; EU-TIRADS categories were never model inputs.
evidence_signal: Among 256 test nodules, including 51 malignant nodules, the descriptor-enhanced model achieved AUROC 0.953 versus 0.948 for EU-TIRADS; at a validation-fixed threshold, it reclassified 72 EU-TIRADS ≥4 false positives as negative while missing two additional cancers.
watch_item: Retrospective, FNA-selected data and reliance on radiologist descriptors warrant prospective external validation before clinical implementation.
paper_title: Fine-tuned Medical Vision-Language Model (MedGemma 1.5 4B) with and without Structured Radiologist Descriptors versus EU-TIRADS for Malignancy Risk Stratification of Thyroid Nodules at Ultrasound: A Tunisian Multicenter Diagnostic Accuracy Study
